If you like liquid staking, you're gonna love liquid chain(s). See you guys on the first liquid EVM 🫡
Liquidity drives block rewards. Block rewards incentivize validators, applications, and users on the chain. Applications and users bring more liquidity into the chain. Rinse and repeat.

And that BGT comes from liquidity provided on whitelisted / governance approved applications and pools on Berachain. The vals directing block rewards towards the most popular pools/apps stand to attract the most BGT, as users hope to compound their own yields.

How does this work in practice? Validators within Berachain's active set have an equal chance of being chosen to produce a block - however, the size of their block reward produced is dependent of the amount of BGT delegated to their validator.
For the first time, a chain's block rewards and distribution of incentives are fundamentally tied to the liquidity flowing across the network, aligning liquidity and security at the protocol level.
Berachain is the first liquid EVM, powered by Proof of Liquidity.

Every degree of freedom offers a universe of new choices. Right now, we're only seeing PoL with the basic chain primitives. I can't even imagine how silly things will get once the hundreds of Bera ecosystem dApps go live, and we get to see Proof of Liquidity in full motion.

But for the first time in a while (and obviously I'm biased here) - while messing with V2 I felt like I was having fun again in crypto beyond shitcoins. I had to figure out which pools to LP - which validators should I delegate to? Where I should post incentives?

It's both invigorating and scary. Berachain is a pretty audacious new experiment in both liquidity and security. There are still a ton of unknown unknowns. We're staring into the abyss, and Proof of Liquidity stares back.

In the coming weeks as on chain governance goes live, validator incentives (previously known as bribes) and BGT fee claims will start distributing to stakers, we'll get to see the full chain in all of its glory.

However, the most exciting portion of all of this is the opportunity to test drive a usable Berachain! With PoL rewards and BGT flowing to pools (don't forget to stake your LP tokens in BGTstation), users finally get to play with the system that we've envisioned for months.
While BeaconKit is still in its infancy, we're excited for its potential to become the gold standard for building EVM blockchains - and for what the eventual BeaconKit ecosystem could look like.

The engineering team put their heads down and got to work on BeaconKit, the base plate for Berachain V2 BeaconKit is the first framework that allows operators to run unmodified execution clients, achieving EVM-Identicality to Ethereum Mainnet with Single Slot Finality.
The V1 mempool was a dark and dangerous place, plagued by known CometBFT issues - causing issues with txn inclusion and the EIP 1559 fee market, leading to all too familiar RPC issues.

The last few months were honestly difficult. We launched V1 with bright eyes and full hearts - and were swiftly smacked in the face by an absolute army of bots, and the technical limitations of Polaris and CometBFT.

Finally, I want to give our deepest thanks to our community who has stuck by us every step of the way, the many many friends of Bera that we've accumulated over the years, our investors, who took a bet on the Beras, the team who makes it all happen, and the builders themselves.

We want the next Uniswap moment for crypto to occur on Berachain. We believe that by aligning incentives between users, developers, and capital providers to solve the practical blockchain trilemma, we have the best chance of making this happen.

Berachain hopes to turbocharge the next class of 0 to 1 applications building on-chain; allowing them to bootstrap their own liquidity and userbase through Proof of Liquidity. Reducing activation energy and escape velocity, and accelerating the next batch of crypto primitives.

A really fair question amongst all of this is: What does Berachain hope to achieve? What's the endgame? In order for crypto to gain true adoption, there have to be many applications which can only be built on-chain. Otherwise folks would simply defer to web2 alternatives.

We've brought on top tier talent with experience leading teams at some of the most successful ecosystems and firms in crypto. I'm especially thankful to my growth team for putting up with my nonsense, and filling the many gaps in my expertise. We would get nowhere without you.

And as the ecosystem has grown to 200+ projects and hundreds of thousands of users, the team has grown with it. We've got Beras in the ground across India, China, MENA, LatAm, and more, with a massive APAC expansion planned over the next few months.

I've been so damn impressed and humbled by the degree of cooperativeness coupled with authenticity that the early ecosystem projects have demonstrated - teaching newcomers that it's perfectly okay to build gamechanging tech while taking themselves less seriously, and having fun.

Culture is often a meme, but as we've travelled from Canada to the US to France, Korea, Singapore, Dubai, Hong Kong and everywhere in between, it's become apparent that it holds true. In every city, you hear an Ooga Booga - and meet dozens of inspired builders.

More importantly, we've seen a torrent of builders approaching us - excited by the prospects of Proof of Liquidity, the incredible appetite from the Berachain community, and the overall culture that's been created here.

Our testnet has shown us just a glimpse of what Proof of Liquidity could enable in the years to come. It quickly became the most active testnet in history, with over 9M users and 130M transactions over the past 3 months (the bots work hard but our screening tools work harder)

We're Berachain. Our goal is to build a chain which aligns incentives between liquidity and security at the protocol level, drives value to the protocols living on top of it, and rewards the users who contribute the most value to the ecosystem.
But along the way, we've never strayed from our mission. We've never chased narratives. We've never pretended to be something different. We are not a parallelized modular zk AI dePIN restaked L3

We've learned a tremendous amount over the past couple of years - we've made lots of mistakes, we've missed lots of opportunities, and we've accepted some of the harsh realities of building something massive in the crypto space.

I've told this story way too many times, but it still feels like just yesterday to me in each case. From multiplying NFTs to the "Berachain is not real" era to rap nights and raising a round as FTX exploded, there's never been a dull moment at Bera HQ.

Berachain has truly grown into something beyond our wildest dreams. When Papa and I were raffling off NFTs of bears with bongs in DeFi Discords in summer '21, there was no Dr. Strange-like scenario that we predicted involving the absolutely hilarious stream of events to follow.

A practical blockchain trilemma consists of 3 pillars - real users, developers, and capital formation. Berachain transforms this into the Proof of Liquidity flywheel. And as of today, we're excited to announce that we've raised $100M co-led by @BHDigitalAssets and @hiframework

tl;dr few VCs and angels are force multipliers. Ohers will waste your time and cycles. I hope the thoughts above are useful esp for new founders navigating investor relations. DM's open for any Q's, and always happy to help people building cool new things. Happy holidays y'all

Naughty: Asking for nonstandard info and gaslighting I know investos who have asked for full cap tables, and breakdowns of an existing round prior to commiting. The former is nonstandard, the latter is not necessary to reveal - it's a choice. Info is leverage. Keep it.

Nice: Helping with recruiting, technical research, marketing Some investors have strong channels for distribution of content - it could be in house research wings or large twitter followings etc. Others are large enough to have in house recruiting. Both are helpful!

Naughty: Committing capital they don't have This one has always been wild to me, but is not uncommon for folks who are in between funds or in the midst of raising their own funds. This leads projects taking investors who can't fund them and nuking investors who could have.

Nice: Helping to fill out a round (post commitment) This should be a standard expectation, esp for leads. If an investor has committed to your round, they should be getting you in front of all their friends and positively backchanneling, if the round isn't already full.

Naughty: Delaying funding post docs There are funds that will purposely take their time to fund a deal, especially if they have relatively low conviction. It shouldn't take more than a week. Exceptions in the case of black swans (FTX, Luna, 3AC etc)

Nice: Proactively offering helpful introductions and ideas The best firms will do their best to help you without you asking for it, while staying out of your way otherwise. Biweekly or monthly mandated meetings etc are useless, but "help when needed" is the ideal meta.

Naughty: Introducing you to other firms mid process This is when a firm lacks conviction or doesn't know a sector. Intro-ing to friends turns it into an all or nothing deal (often nothing). If a firm wants the deal, they'll fill before they shill. Some nuance here re: stage.

Nice: Running a tight and clear process It's rare to take more than 2-3 weeks in DD (a little more for deep cryptography etc). Most firms know if they want to do a deal within 2-3 meetings max. Good firms will tell you their steps and timelines and hit them.

Alrighty let's kick it off Naughty: Asking for advisory tokens upon investing (or even worse, after committing to invest but prior to signing docs) Oldest trick in the book to lower cost basis. Advisor tokens are earned, not given. Fair game to ask after helping.

A lot of founders end up being subject to crappy behaviour from VCs - things that wouldn't pass in Web2 VC but have somehow become standard in Web3, and then just general stuff that all VCs do But it's easy to not know when a VC is pulling some sus crap on you

We all know that crypto is a pretty young industry - this also comes with a ton of first time founders. The space is an inefficient market that attracts the best and worst types of people - some that want to make the market better, others that want to extract value

And finally, thank you to our investors for trusting a fake chain run by anonymous jpegs of bears smoking weed with your capital. We've got a lot of honey to spread, and with your help, it's looking more and more possible by the day.

the only mfs crazy enough to string together dozens of projects into a game that had trad VCs asking me about it in the middle of a bank run, while minting out 16,420 NFTs. I treasure all of you wonderful wacky characters, armies of Bera alts, and the cult of Bera that's formed.

There are too many of you all to name, but I'll make special shoutouts to @ohmzeus who decided to sweep the bears on mint, and has repped the cause with pride, and @deepname99, the first of the illustrious cult of bera janitors who then assembled the motley crew of @0xhoneyjar -

And perhaps more than anything else, it's coming together because of the community - the thousands of crazy mfs creating pastas on Discord and building dapps without even a testnet The original VC crew, the guys who played Warzone with Dev, the folks who know Papa exists!

This is all coming together because of the hard work from Papa, @itsdevbear @ab0xDD @cal__bera @DevLobster @0xSami_ @DefinedNever @missionbera @0xCorduroy @lumpsoull and many other bera team members that are smart enough to stay off Twitter.

I wish I could take credit for even half of the ideas and vision that I've mentioned. But I just do the henlos and the ooga boogas. The Berachain vision is the culmination of months of iteration, sleepless nights, empty Red Bulls and scribbles on whiteboards from the whole team.

We've got the opportunity to draw in assets from every EVM and Cosmos chain to build the deepest and most capital efficient pools in existence, giving users all of the depth and velocity of capital of a CEX combined with the transparency and customizable nature of an on-chain eco

systematically building liquidity incentivizing protocols and validators to engage in chain infrastructure redefining the cost of corruption solving stake centralization Berachain takes swings at some of the biggest problems in DeFi, and within the blockchain space as a whole

dapps can leverage this liquidity routing environment to bootstrap their own ecosystem and contracts Berachain becomes the first chain to bootstrap liquidity for its builders and flip the current dominant meta of grants & fake ecosystem funds

with the fees from these core "app-chain"-like primitives accruing value to the protocol layer, we see the start of a flywheel incentivizing protocols and validators to participate in network governance and liquidity provision with tangible incentives - the Fat Bera Thesis

an elegant system, allowing for multiple sources of permissioned capital contributing to network security to simultaneously serve as a source of productive liquidity feeding into a set of DeFi legos: a spot AMM, a perpetual futures exchange, and a stablecoin lending platform

and they became the perfect group to talk to as we validated our theses and explored what retail participants and developers valued in an on-chain ecosystem. with feedback from the community and many long hours with Papa, Dev and Homme, Proof of Liquidity was born.

as we were coming to this realization, the beras were picking up steam. we had accidentally bootstrapped a community of thousands of brilliant yet smooth brained DeFi lovers who were risk-on enough to buy jpegs of bears smoking weed for god knows what reason

at the same time, we saw multiple ecosystems with 7 figs in TVL across the entire chain, with 100x more sitting with validators without a doubt, the network was secure - but at what cost? liquidity truly is the lifeblood of defi, and beyond that, protocol activity

no matter how decentralized, scalable or secure these chains were - no matter how great the time to finality was and no matter how interoperable etc; if there wasn't liquidity present, the chain quickly became a ghost town

we saw the rise and fall of a number of chains and ecosystems, and spent a considerable amount of time in the alt-L1 rotation over 2021 and 2022. a common cycle played out - chain launches > ecosystem fund > dex & maybe lending market > TVL pump > emissions dry up > chain ded

It's been a whirlwind journey, and this is just the beginning for Berachain. But first, a sentimental history lesson from Smokey the Bera. Papa and I have been investing in crypto since 2015 - we seeded deals in 2017/18, played all the shitcoins, and hopped into DeFi summer.

Over a year and a half ago, Papa and I were joking about making NFTs of bears smoking weed. And today, we're announcing that we've raised $42.0M from some of the best crypto investors and angels in the game to build the first protocol which truly aligns liquidity and security.
